summary: Intro discovery focused on Elmwood Bank's regulatory constraints. Primary ask: ensure EU-only data residency for certain products and strict logging controls for PII and payment data. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, KMS/HSM options, and audit log retention. Agreed to follow up with technical deep-dive and pilots.
transcript:
[2026-03-04 15:00] Meeting start
Header: 2026-03-04 15:00 EST | Duration 45m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Carlos (Elmwood CTO), Meera (Head of Compliance), Derek (Infra)

Summary: quick intros, then Meera takes us through compliance baseline; Carlos and Derek talk infra. Priya explains Redwood hosting modes and controls. Lots of back-and-forth on logging and key ownership.

[15:02] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round robin? we'll keep to 30-40, we have a few items — data residency, logging, and KMS.
[15:03] Carlos: yep, thanks. Elmwood's rolling out a conversational assistant for banking support, targeted at EU and US users. primary concern for us is data residency for EU customers and strict non-retention of certain tokens.
[15:03] Meera: and I'll jump in — compliance is looking for GDPR controls, ability to demonstrate data processing agreements, also we have some PCI scope and GLBA considerations. we also need to know about audit logs — we cannot have raw PII in logs for EU users.
[15:04] Priya: got it. quick high level: Redwood offers three deployment modes — Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in cloud regions), and Private (VPC/private control plane, and on-prem option). For EU-only residency we can route requests to EU regions and for Dedicated we can provision capacity in eu-west-1, or do Private if you need the control plane in your network.
[15:05] Derek: can you clarify the difference between Dedicated and Private? specifically around where logs land and who has access to encryption keys?
[15:06] Priya: sure — Dedicated is still a Redwood-managed control plane but you get a reserved pool of capacity and isolation; logs and traces can be configured with retention and redaction rules, and we support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest for Dedicated in some contracts. Private gives you the option to run the control plane in your VPC or on-prem — keys stay with you, network egress is controlled, and we can disable or limit telemetry to meet strict audit requirements.
[15:07] Meera: so for GDPR we need data processing agreements, sub-processors list, and ideally a contractual commitment that EU data stays in EU. Also, can we prevent prompts from being stored? even ephemeral logs need PII redaction.
[15:08] Jordan: yes, we have a standard DPA that includes EU data residency options and subprocessors. we can offer a clause for EU-only storage and we have S3 buckets in eu-west-1 that are used for customer data when you select EU residency. as for prompt storage, we support configurable retention, and we can disable long-term storage — short-term ephemeral logs for debugging only, with options to turn off.
[15:09] Meera: how about token-level logs? we need to show auditors that we don't keep full prompts for X months.
[15:09] Priya: right, so we provide token-level usage metrics for billing and aggregate telemetry, but full prompt retention is configurable. for Dedicated/Private we can set retention to 0 or retention < 7 days and do automatic redaction of detected PII. detection isn't perfect, so we recommend a redact-then-store pipeline and we can integrate with your PII redaction service.
[15:10] Derek: interesting. what about KMS? we want customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or an HSM. is that supported?
[15:11] Priya: yes — for Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS keys in certain regions (we'll get legal to sign off) and Private gives you full HSM/KMS control. we also support envelope encryption patterns so logs and artifacts are encrypted with your key.
[15:12] Carlos: latency impact when using Private or customer-managed KMS? we have a sub-second SLO for lookups on some flows.
[15:12] Priya: good callout. Private on-prem can reduce network hops but depends on your infra. customer-managed KMS adds a round-trip for key operations if not cached; we use envelope encryption to minimize KMS calls in the critical path, so encryption overhead is small. Dedicated in-region is usually the sweet spot for predictable latency with contractual SLAs.
[15:13] Meera: a couple of questions — HIPAA applies to some of our partners; we don't handle protected health info ourselves but partners might. do you have any HIPAA controls or BAA?
[15:14] Jordan: Redwood has customers in regulated industries and we have a BAA available for certain deployments. HIPAA controls map to our audit logging, encryption, access control policies. we'll send the legal team the template BAA.
[15:15] Meera: perfect. also auditors will want to see SOC2, ISO and pen test reports.
[15:15] Jordan: yes — we'll share our SOC2 Type II report and pen test summary.
[15:16] Derek: about logging — can we disable request/response logging entirely for certain routes, or mask specific fields?
[15:16] Priya: you can configure per-route logging policies — disable storing responses, redact fields by JSON path, and we have token filters. we also have a live masking feature for sensitive attributes; note that some debugging metadata may remain in ephemeral traces unless you disable tracing.
[15:17] Carlos: for PCI scope, anything that touches cardholder data could bring us into a bigger scope. Can Redwood sign an agreement to never persist raw card numbers and support field-level tokenization?
[15:18] Priya: we can advise on architectural patterns — best practice is to never send raw card numbers to the model; our SDKs can integrate with your tokenization service so the model only receives tokens. we can also set strict redaction rules and filter patterns for card-like strings. we can include language in contract about non-retention of certain patterns, but auditors will want to see the implementation too.
[15:19] Meera: ok — and can we self-host the model weights? some of our security team prefers weights on-prem for certain models.
[15:19] Priya: Private on-prem supports that; we can run a private renderer and model weights behind your firewall. note that model updates and patches will be handled via a controlled process; there's operational overhead. Dedicated cannot host customer-owned weights, but we can run curated models in your VPC under certain agreements.
[15:20] Jordan: I just want to call out a few common tradeoffs — Hosted is fastest to integrate but least control; Dedicated gives you capacity and regional guarantees with moderate control; Private on-prem gives maximal control but more ops.
[15:21] Carlos: what's the timeline and cost for a Dedicated pilot — say 2 r5-like GPU nodes for a month?
[15:21] Priya: I'll get an estimate — depends on model and quantization. for a small pilot we usually recommend a burst-able Dedicated pool; I'll calculate cost/latency for your 500 TPS peak and send the numbers.
[15:22] Meera: auditors will ask about identity — SSO/SAML, RBAC, and admin audit trails. can we integrate with our Okta and set role mappings?
[15:23] Priya: yes — SAML SSO is supported, and we have RBAC roles (admin, dev, auditor). audit trails are available and can be exported to your SIEM. for Private you can forward logs to your Splunk/Elastic stack.
[15:24] Derek: for data residency enforcement — how do you prevent routing to non-EU regions in edge cases?
[15:24] Priya: we have smart routing policies; you can require region-locked endpoints and fail closed if capacity isn't available in the selected region. plus, network egress policies in Private mode prevent accidental routing. we'll include region-locking in the DPA and SLOs for Dedicated.
[15:25] Meera: what's your retention default today? 30 days? and can we get it to zero?
[15:25] Jordan: default is 30 days for debugging, aggregated metrics retained longer. yes — for Dedicated/Private we can set prompt retention to 0 or minimal and have redaction hooks. we'll need to document the expected operational impact (harder to debug).
[15:26] Carlos: any regulatory certifications for the EU? ISO/IEC 27001?
[15:26] Jordan: we have SOC2 and are pursuing ISO; I'll check exact scope and dates for ISO certificates.
[15:27] Meera: ok sounds promising. a few follow-ups from our side: we'll need a quick tech doc that spells out the data flows, plus a legal DPA and BAA draft.
[15:28] Jordan: will do. Priya, anything to add before we wrap?
[15:29] Priya: just to reiterate — we'll prepare the technical deep-dive agenda: 1) infra diagram review, 2) Dedicated capacity sizing and region options, 3) KMS/HSM integration patterns, 4) logging/redaction walkthrough, and 5) pilot success criteria and SLOs.
[15:30] Derek: one last practical Q — can we run a small benchmark with our sample data to validate latency and quality without sending PII? maybe use anonymized prompts?
[15:31] Priya: absolutely — we can run a bench with sanitized prompts or within Private pilot. Jordan will coordinate.
[15:32] Jordan: recap of next steps: I'll send SOC2 + DPA + BAA templates; Priya will produce cost/latency pilot estimate; Derek will send infra diagram; we'll schedule the technical deep dive next week. action owners on the notes.
[15:33] Meera: thanks all.
[15:34] Carlos: thanks.
[15:35] Meeting end
questions: Can Redwood guarantee EU-only storage and region locking?
Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS/HSM for Dedicated and Private?
Can prompt/response logging be disabled or redacted for PCI/PII sensitive routes?
